name: Heme degradation (bilirubin)
summary: Old red cells are broken down by macrophages (spleen): heme → biliverdin → unconjugated bilirubin, carried on albumin to the liver, conjugated with glucuronic acid (UGT1A1) and pumped into bile (MRP2, rate-limiting). Gut bacteria make urobilinogen: most leaves as stercobilin (brown stool); some is reabsorbed and leaves in urine as urobilin (yellow). Unconjugated ↑: hemolysis, Gilbert, Crigler-Najjar, newborns. Conjugated ↑: Dubin-Johnson, Rotor, biliary obstruction (pale stool, dark urine, no urine urobilinogen).

heme.name: Heme
heme.notes: From hemoglobin of senescent red cells (and myoglobin, cytochromes).

biliverdin.name: Biliverdin
biliverdin.notes: Green (the green of a healing bruise).

ubili.name: Unconjugated bilirubin
ubili.notes: Yellow and fat-soluble: travels bound to albumin, isn't filtered by the kidney (no bilirubinuria), and in newborns can cross the blood-brain barrier (kernicterus).

ubilil.name: Unconjugated bilirubin (liver)
ubilil.notes: Taken up from albumin into the hepatocyte.

cbili.name: Conjugated bilirubin
cbili.notes: Water-soluble: when it backs up into blood it appears in urine (dark urine).

urobilinogen.name: Urobilinogen
urobilinogen.notes: About 20% is reabsorbed (enterohepatic circulation); a little reaches the kidney. Absent from urine in complete biliary obstruction; ↑ in hemolysis.

stercobilin.name: Stercobilin
stercobilin.notes: Brown color of stool. Pale (clay-colored) stool when bile can't reach the gut.

ho.name: Heme oxygenase
ho.notes: In macrophages (spleen, liver, bone marrow). Releases iron (recycled via ferritin/transferrin) and carbon monoxide (the body's only source).

alb.name: Albumin (blood) and hepatic uptake
alb.notes: Unconjugated bilirubin rides on albumin; drugs like sulfonamides can displace it (kernicterus risk in newborns).

ugt.name: UDP-glucuronosyltransferase
ugt.notes: Gilbert syndrome: mildly ↓ (unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia with fasting, stress, illness; benign). Crigler-Najjar type I: absent (severe jaundice, kernicterus; liver transplant). Type II: ↓ (milder; responds to phenobarbital, which induces UGT). Newborns: immature UGT → physiologic jaundice (treat with phototherapy).

mrp2.name: MRP2 (bile canalicular pump)
mrp2.notes: Rate-limiting step of bilirubin excretion. Dubin-Johnson: defective MRP2 → conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, black liver. Rotor: milder, liver not black.

gut.name: Gut bacteria (reduction)
gut.notes: Bacteria deconjugate and reduce bilirubin. Newborns lack them, and antibiotics reduce them.
